newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS AS TOMBA CRASHES OUT.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS AS TOMBA CRASHES OUT.

text.p: Austrian Thomas Sykora won a special three-legged floodlit slalom and a $35,000 prize on Wednesday after Italy's Alberto Tomba straddled a gate, crashed and withdrew from the race.
Sykora's winning time -- combining the fastest two of the three legs -- was one minute 18.08 seconds.
The Austrian, skiing beautifully on the edges of his skis through the 36 gates, was fastest in his second and third runs after being fourth in the first leg.
Compatriot Thomas Stangassinger was second in 1:19.59 while Norwegian Tom Stiansen was third in 1:19.91.
The race, organised by the Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper, was on the same piste that hosts the Alpine skiing world championships in one month's time.
But the course, over 500 metres with a vertical drop of 140 metres, was shorter than the championship slalom which will also be held at night but in the usual two-leg format.

Tomba, determined to impress his home fans this year after skiing out in two of the legs in the first version of the race staged last January, straddled a gate near the finish on his first run and then crashed out on his second.
"The piste was really hard and the ice is unforgiving," he said. "I was using too much power, I was getting faster when I went out. The same thing happened last year."

The double world and triple Olympic champion said later that a screw had sheared on his left ski in the second run. That left his boot still attached to the plate but without a ski, which careered off at a tangent.
Tomba fell heavily and seemed as incredulous as he was angry when he got to his feet, face covered in snow.
The slalom was only Tomba's second race of the season after he injured a knee and a wrist in training in October.
Tomba said that he had bruised his right hand in Wednesday night's fall but not seriously.

However the knock, to his pride as much as anything, was enough to prevent him from racing a third leg when there was no longer anything to be gained by it. "There's a sheet of ice appeared on the piste and its become risky," he said.
"As usual I've started the season badly," continued the Italian, who nonetheless came second in his only World Cup race of the season at Madonna di Campiglio last month.
"But from tonight I'll start drinking and get charged up," he joked. "I should have started drinking last night."
Tomba's next World Cup race is a slalom and giant slalom in Kranjska Gora, Slovenia, on Sunday and Monday.
